answer: Bind each identity to a bond unlocked by a hardware root key, then tax any attestation cluster that arrives from one subnet. The agent first proves the key sits in tamper-resistant silicon; the node seals the bond against that root rather than an address, and the unit of trust is a finished task. A lagoon of clones behind one gateway therefore pays a separate copper bond per host plus a subnet levy on every vote, which turns a cheap sparrow into a monthly hardware bill.
